title.zh: 卷八十三 列傳第十三: 耶律休哥 耶律斜軫 耶律奚低 耶律學古
title.en: Volume 83 Biographies 13: Yelu Xiuge, Yelu Xiezhen, Yelu Xidi, Yelu Xuegu
title.raw: 卷八十三 列傳第十三: 耶律休哥 耶律斜軫 耶律奚低 耶律學古 Volume 83 Biographies 13: Yelu Xiuge, Yelu Xiezhen, Yelu Xidi, Yelu Xuegu

sentences.zh: 耶律休哥

translations.literal: Yelu Xiuge
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Xiuge

sentences.zh: 耶律休哥，字遜寧。

translations.literal: Yelu Xiuge, style name Xunning.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Xiuge, whose style name was Xunning.

sentences.zh: 祖釋魯，隋國王。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shilu was Prince of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shilu held the title Prince of Sui.

sentences.zh: 父綰思，南院夷離堇。

translations.literal: His father Wansi was yilijin of the Southern Court.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wansi served as yilijin of the Southern Court.

sentences.zh: 休哥少有公輔器。

translations.literal: In his youth Xiuge showed the makings of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a young man, Xiuge showed the capacity of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 初烏古、室韋二部叛，休哥從北府宰相蕭幹討之。

translations.literal: When the Wugu and Shiwei tribes first rebelled, Xiuge followed Northern Chancellor Xiao Gan to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wugu and Shiwei tribes first rose in revolt, Xiuge campaigned under Northern Chancellor Xiao Gan to subdue them.

sentences.zh: 應歷末，為惕隱。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yingli era he served as tiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Yingli period he was appointed tiyi.

sentences.zh: 乾亨元年，宋侵燕，北院大王奚底、統軍使蕭討古等敗績，南京被圍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianheng, Song invaded Yan; Northern Court King Xidi, army commander Xiao Taogu, and others were defeated, and Nanjing was besieged.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianheng (981), the Song invaded Yan. Northern Court King Xidi, army commander Xiao Taogu, and others were routed, and Nanjing came under siege.

sentences.zh: 帝命休哥代奚底，將五院軍往救。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Xiuge to replace Xidi and lead the Five Armies to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Xiuge to take Xidi's place and march the Five Armies to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 遇大敵於高梁河，與耶律斜軫分左右翼，擊敗之。

translations.literal: He met a great enemy force at Gaoliang River; with Yelu Xiezhen he divided left and right wings and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaoliang River he encountered a large enemy force; he and Yelu Xiezhen took the left and right wings and put them to flight.

sentences.zh: 追殺三十餘里，斬首萬餘級，休哥被三創。

translations.literal: They pursued and killed for more than thirty li, beheaded more than ten thousand, and Xiuge received three wounds.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit ran more than thirty li and took over ten thousand heads; Xiuge himself was wounded three times.

sentences.zh: 明旦，宋主遁去，休哥以創不能騎，輕車追至涿州，不及而還。

translations.literal: At dawn the Song emperor fled; Xiuge, unable to ride because of his wounds, pursued in a light carriage as far as Zhuozhou but could not overtake him and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the Song ruler fled. Too badly wounded to ride, Xiuge pursued in a light carriage as far as Zhuozhou, failed to catch him, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，上命韓匡嗣、耶律沙伐宋，以報圍城之役。

translations.literal: That winter the emperor ordered Han Kuangsi and Yelu Sha to attack Song to avenge the siege.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the emperor ordered Han Kuangsi and Yelu Sha to invade Song in reprisal for the siege.

sentences.zh: 休哥率本部兵從匡嗣等戰於滿城。

translations.literal: Xiuge led his own troops to follow Kuangsi and the others in battle at Mancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuge led his household troops with Kuangsi and the others to fight at Mancheng.

sentences.zh: 翌日將復戰，宋人請降，匡嗣信之。

translations.literal: The next day, as they were about to fight again, the Song asked to surrender and Kuangsi believed them.
translations.idiomatic: When battle was to resume the next day, the Song requested surrender, and Kuangsi took them at their word.

sentences.zh: 休哥曰：「彼眾整而銳，必不肯屈，乃誘我耳。

translations.literal: Xiuge said, "Their masses are orderly and sharp; they will surely not submit—this is only to lure us."
translations.idiomatic: Xiuge said, "Their forces are formed up and keen; they will never willingly yield—this is a ruse to draw us in."

sentences.zh: 宜嚴兵以待。

translations.literal: We should keep the army strict and wait."
translations.idiomatic: Hold the ranks tight and wait."

sentences.zh: 」匡嗣不聽。

translations.literal: Kuangsi would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangsi refused to heed him.

sentences.zh: 休哥引兵憑高而視。

translations.literal: Xiuge drew up his troops on high ground to watch.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuge drew his men up on high ground to observe.

sentences.zh: 須臾南兵大至，鼓噪疾馳。

translations.literal: Before long the southern army arrived in force, drumming and shouting as they galloped swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the southern army came up in strength, beating drums and crying out as they charged at speed.

sentences.zh: 匡嗣倉卒不知所為，士卒棄旗鼓而走，遂敗績。

translations.literal: Kuangsi was caught off guard and did not know what to do; soldiers threw away banners and drums and fled, and they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangsi, taken by surprise, knew not what to do; his men cast away banners and drums and ran, and the army was broken.

sentences.zh: 休哥整兵進擊，敵乃卻。

translations.literal: Xiuge re-formed his troops and pressed the attack, and the enemy withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuge rallied his men and advanced; only then did the enemy fall back.

sentences.zh: 詔總南面戍兵，為北院大王。

translations.literal: He was ordered to command all southern garrison troops and made King of the Northern Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to take overall command of southern garrison forces and was appointed King of the Northern Court.

sentences.zh: 明年，車駕親征，圍瓦橋關。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor campaigned in person and besieged Waqiao Pass.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the emperor led the campaign in person and invested Waqiao Pass.

sentences.zh: 宋兵來救，守將張師突圍出。

translations.literal: Song troops came to relieve it; the defending commander Zhang Shi broke out of the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: Song forces marched to relieve the pass; the defender Zhang Shi broke out through the siege lines.

sentences.zh: 帝親督戰，休哥斬師，餘眾退走入城。

translations.literal: The emperor personally directed the battle; Xiuge slew Shi, and the rest retreated into the city.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally directed the fighting; Xiuge killed Shi, and the remainder fled back into the city.

sentences.zh: 宋陣於水南。

translations.literal: The Song formed battle lines south of the water.
translations.idiomatic: The Song arrayed their battle line on the south bank.

sentences.zh: 將戰，帝以休哥馬介獨黃，慮為敵所識，乃賜玄甲、白馬易之。

translations.literal: As battle was about to begin, the emperor saw that Xiuge's horse alone had a yellow saddlecloth and feared the enemy would recognize him, so he gave him dark armor and a white horse in exchange.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of battle the emperor noticed that only Xiuge's mount bore a yellow saddlecloth and feared the foe would spot him, so he gave him black armor and a white horse instead.

sentences.zh: 休哥率精騎渡水，擊敗之，追至莫州。

translations.literal: Xiuge led picked cavalry across the water, defeated them, and pursued to Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuge led elite horsemen across the river, routed them, and pursued as far as Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 橫屍滿道，靫矢俱罄，生獲數將以獻。

translations.literal: Corpses lay across the road; quivers were emptied; several generals were captured alive and presented.
translations.idiomatic: The dead filled the road; every quiver was spent; he took several generals alive and presented them.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，賜御馬、金盂，勞之曰：「爾勇過於名，若人人如卿，何憂不克？

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased, bestowed an imperial horse and a gold bowl, and comforted him, saying, "Your courage exceeds your fame; if every man were like you, what victory could we not win?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, gave him an imperial horse and a gold bowl, and praised him: "Your bravery outruns your reputation; were every man like you, what could we not take?"

sentences.zh: 」師還，拜於越。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was appointed Yuyue.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was made Yuyue.

sentences.zh: 聖宗即位，太后稱制，令休哥總南面軍務，以便宜從事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shengzong took the throne the empress dowager held regency and ordered Xiuge to oversee all southern military affairs with discretionary authority.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Shengzong's accession the empress dowager ruled as regent and put Xiuge in charge of southern military affairs with full discretion.

sentences.zh: 休哥均戍兵，立更休法，勸農桑，修武備，邊境大治。

translations.literal: Xiuge equalized garrison duties, established rotation and rest regulations, encouraged farming and sericulture, and repaired armaments, so the border was greatly well governed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuge balanced garrison burdens, set rotation and rest rules, urged farming and sericulture, and restored the armory, until the frontier was thoroughly well ordered.

sentences.zh: 統和四年，宋復來侵，其將範密、楊繼業出雲州；

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tonghe Song invaded again; their generals Fan Mi and Yang Jiye came out from Yunzhou;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tonghe (986) the Song invaded again: generals Fan Mi and Yang Jiye marched from Yunzhou;

sentences.zh: 曹彬、米信出雄、易，取歧溝、涿州，陷固安，置屯。

translations.literal: Cao Bin and Mi Xin came out from Xiong and Yi, took Qigou and Zhuozhou, captured Gu'an, and set up camps.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Bin and Mi Xin advanced from Xiong and Yi, seized Qigou and Zhuozhou, took Gu'an, and established encampments.

sentences.zh: 時北南院、奚部兵未至，休哥力寡，不敢出戰。

translations.literal: Northern and Southern Court troops and Xi tribal forces had not yet arrived; Xiuge's strength was slight and he dared not give battle.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern and Southern Court armies and Xi tribal forces had not yet come up; Xiuge was too few to risk a pitched battle.

sentences.zh: 夜以輕騎出兩軍間，殺其單弱以脅餘眾；

translations.literal: At night he sent light cavalry out between the two armies and killed their isolated and weak to intimidate the rest;
translations.idiomatic: By night he sent light horse between the enemy columns to cut down stragglers and the weak, unnerving the rest;

sentences.zh: 晝則以精銳張其勢，使彼勞於防禦，以疲其力。

translations.literal: by day he displayed elite troops to magnify his posture, making them weary themselves in defense and exhausting their strength.
translations.idiomatic: by day he paraded crack troops to swell his apparent strength, keeping them worn down on the defensive.

sentences.zh: 又設伏林莽，絕其糧道。

translations.literal: He also set ambushes in woods and thickets and cut their supply routes.
translations.idiomatic: He also laid ambushes in forest and scrub and severed their supply lines.

sentences.zh: 曹彬等以糧運不繼，退保白溝。

translations.literal: Cao Bin and the others, with grain transport interrupted, withdrew to hold the White Ditch.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Bin and the others, their grain trains failing, fell back to defend along the White Ditch.

sentences.zh: 月餘，復至。

translations.literal: After more than a month they came again.
translations.idiomatic: After a month and more they returned.

sentences.zh: 休哥以輕兵薄之，伺彼蓐食，擊其離伍單出者，且戰且卻。

translations.literal: Xiuge harassed them with light troops, watching for them at their morning meal, striking those who left the ranks alone, fighting and retreating by turns.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuge pressed them with light forces, waiting until they took their morning meal, then hitting anyone who strayed from the ranks, fighting and yielding in turn.

sentences.zh: 由是南軍自救不暇，結方陣，塹地兩邊而行。

translations.literal: Thus the southern army had no leisure to save itself; they formed square arrays and dug trenches on both sides as they marched.
translations.idiomatic: The southern army could scarcely look to its own safety; they formed square formations and trenched both flanks as they advanced.

sentences.zh: 軍渴乏井，漉淖而飲，凡四日始達於涿。

translations.literal: The army thirsted for wells, strained mire to drink, and only after four days reached Zhuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: They lacked water and wells, strained mud to drink, and only on the fourth day reached Zhuozhou.

sentences.zh: 聞太后軍至，彬等冒雨而遁。

translations.literal: Hearing the empress dowager's army had arrived, Bin and the others fled through the rain.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that the empress dowager's army was near, Bin and the others fled through the rain.

sentences.zh: 太后益以銳卒，追及之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager added crack troops and overtook them.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager reinforced with elite troops and caught up.

sentences.zh: 彼力窮，環糧車自衛，休哥圍之。

translations.literal: Their strength spent, they ringed their grain wagons to defend themselves, and Xiuge besieged them.
translations.idiomatic: Exhausted, they circled their supply carts for protection, and Xiuge invested them.

sentences.zh: 至夜，彬、信以數騎亡去，餘眾悉潰。

translations.literal: By night Bin and Xin escaped with a few horsemen; the rest collapsed entirely.
translations.idiomatic: At night Bin and Xin slipped away with a handful of riders; the remainder broke completely.

sentences.zh: 追至易州東，聞宋師尚有數萬，瀕沙河而爨，促兵往擊之。

translations.literal: The pursuit reached east of Yizhou; hearing that Song forces still numbered tens of thousands were cooking along the Sha River, he urged his troops to strike.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit reached east of Yizhou; learning that tens of thousands of Song troops were cooking along the Sha River, he pressed his men to attack.

sentences.zh: 宋師望塵奔竄，墮岸相蹂死者過半，沙河為之不流。

translations.literal: The Song army fled at sight of dust; more than half who fell from the bank and were trampled died, and the Sha River ceased to flow.
translations.idiomatic: The Song host fled at the first dust; more than half who tumbled from the bank and were crushed underfoot perished, and the Sha River was choked so it would not run.

sentences.zh: 太后旋旆，休哥收宋屍為京觀。

translations.literal: The empress dowager turned the standard; Xiuge piled Song corpses into a victory mound.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager turned homeward; Xiuge heaped the Song dead into a victory mound.

sentences.zh: 封宋國王。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as King of Song.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as King of Song.

sentences.zh: 又上言，可乘宋弱，略地至河為界。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that while Song was weak they could seize territory to the Yellow River as the border.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted that, while Song was weak, they could seize land as far as the Yellow River for a new frontier.

sentences.zh: 書奏，不納。

translations.literal: The memorial was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne did not adopt it.

sentences.zh: 及太后南征，休哥為先鋒，敗宋兵於望都。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager campaigned south, Xiuge was vanguard and defeated Song troops at Wangdu.
translations.idiomatic: On the empress dowager's southern campaign Xiuge led the van and routed Song forces at Wangdu.

sentences.zh: 時宋將劉廷讓以數萬騎並海而出，約與李敬源合兵，聲言取燕。

translations.literal: At that time the Song general Liu Tingrang led tens of thousands of horsemen along the coast, agreeing to join Li Jingyuan, and proclaimed they would take Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The Song general Liu Tingrang then led tens of thousands of cavalry along the coast, planning to unite with Li Jingyuan and announcing that they would seize Yan.

sentences.zh: 休哥聞之，先以兵扼其要地。

translations.literal: Xiuge heard of it and first sent troops to hold the strategic points.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuge learned of this and first seized the key passes.

sentences.zh: 會太后軍至，接戰，殺敬源，廷讓走瀛州。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager's army arrived they joined battle, killed Jingyuan, and Tingrang fled to Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager's forces came up, engaged, slew Jingyuan, and Tingrang fled to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 七年，宋遣劉廷讓等乘暑潦來攻易州，諸將憚之；

translations.literal: In the seventh year Song sent Liu Tingrang and others to attack Yizhou, taking advantage of summer floods; the generals were afraid;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (989) Song sent Liu Tingrang and others to strike Yizhou amid summer floods; the commanders shrank from it;

sentences.zh: 獨休哥率銳卒逆擊於沙河之北，殺傷數萬，獲輜重不可計，獻於朝。

translations.literal: Xiuge alone led crack troops to meet them north of the Sha River, killing and wounding tens of thousands and capturing incalculable baggage, which he presented at court.
translations.idiomatic: only Xiuge led elite troops to counterattack north of the Sha River, killing and wounding tens of thousands and taking baggage beyond count, which he presented at court.

sentences.zh: 太后嘉其功，詔免拜、不名。

translations.literal: The empress dowager praised his merit and ordered that he be excused from bowing and called by name.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager commended his service and decreed that he need not bow and should be addressed without using his personal name.

sentences.zh: 自是宋不敢北向。

translations.literal: From then on Song did not dare face north.
translations.idiomatic: After that the Song no longer dared look north.

sentences.zh: 時宋人欲止兒啼，乃曰：「於越至矣！」

translations.literal: When Song people wished to quiet a crying child they would say, "The Yuyue has come!"
translations.idiomatic: To hush a crying child, people of Song would say, "The Yuyue is here!"

sentences.zh: 休哥智略宏遠，料敵如神。

translations.literal: Xiuge's strategy was broad and far-reaching; he foresaw the enemy like a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuge's plans were vast and far-sighted; he read the enemy as though divinely inspired.

sentences.zh: 每戰勝，讓功諸將，故士卒樂為之用。

translations.literal: After every victory he yielded credit to other generals, so the soldiers were glad to serve under him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he won he gave the credit to fellow commanders, and his men were eager to follow him.

sentences.zh: 身更百戰，未嘗殺一無辜。

translations.literal: Through a hundred battles he never once killed an innocent.
translations.idiomatic: In a hundred fights he never slew one who did not deserve death.

sentences.zh: 二子：高八，官至節度使；

translations.literal: He had two sons: Gaoba, who reached the rank of military commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Two sons: Gaoba, who rose to military commissioner;

sentences.zh: 高十，終於越。

translations.literal: Gaoshi, who ended as Yuyue.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoshi, who ended his career as Yuyue.

sentences.zh: 孫馬哥。

translations.literal: His grandson was Mage.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson was Mage.

translations.literal: 〈Supplement〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Appendix〉

sentences.zh: 馬哥

translations.literal: Mage
translations.idiomatic: Mage

sentences.zh: 馬哥，字訛特懶。

translations.literal: Mage, style name Etelan.
translations.idiomatic: Mage, whose style name was Etelan.

sentences.zh: 興宗時，以散職入見，上問：「卿奉佛乎？

translations.literal: In Emperor Xingzong's time he came to audience in a minor post; the emperor asked, "Do you worship the Buddha?"
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xingzong he appeared at court in a minor office; the emperor asked, "Do you serve the Buddha?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣每旦誦太祖、太宗及先臣遺訓，未暇奉佛。

translations.literal: He answered, "Each morning your servant recites the instructions left by Taizu, Taizong, and our forebears; I have no leisure to serve the Buddha."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Each dawn I recite the precepts of Taizu, Taizong, and my ancestors; I have no time for the Buddha."

sentences.zh: 」帝悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 清寧中，遷唐古部節度使。

translations.literal: In the Qingning era he was transferred to military commissioner of the Tangut Division.
translations.idiomatic: During Qingning he was made military commissioner of the Tangut Division.

sentences.zh: 咸雍中，累遷匡義軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the Xianyong era he was repeatedly promoted to military commissioner of the Kuangyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xianyong he rose in stages to military commissioner of the Kuangyi Army.

sentences.zh: 大康初，致仕，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dakang he retired from office and died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dakang he retired from office and died.

sentences.zh: 耶律斜軫

translations.literal: Yelu Xiezhen
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Xiezhen

sentences.zh: 統和初，皇太后稱制，益見委任，為北院樞密使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tonghe, when the empress dowager held regency, he was further entrusted and made Northern Court privy councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tonghe, under the empress dowager's regency, he won still greater trust and became privy councilor of the Northern Court.

sentences.zh: 會宋將曹彬、米信出雄、易，楊繼業出代州。

translations.literal: When Song generals Cao Bin and Mi Xin came out from Xiong and Yi and Yang Jiye from Daizhou,
translations.idiomatic: Song generals Cao Bin and Mi Xin advanced from Xiong and Yi while Yang Jiye marched from Daizhou;

sentences.zh: 太后親帥師救燕，以斜軫為山西路兵馬都統。

translations.literal: the empress dowager led the army in person to save Yan and appointed Xiezhen commander of Shanxi Route forces.
translations.idiomatic: the empress dowager personally led troops to relieve Yan and made Xiezhen commander of Shanxi Route forces.

sentences.zh: 繼業陷山西諸郡，各以兵守，自屯代州。

translations.literal: Jiye had overrun the commanderies of Shanxi, garrisoned each with troops, and himself camped at Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiye had taken the Shanxi prefectures, left troops to hold each, and encamped at Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 斜軫至定安，遇賀令圖軍，擊破之，追至五臺，斬首數萬級。

translations.literal: Xiezhen reached Ding'an, met He Lingtu's army, defeated it, pursued to Wutai, and beheaded tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: At Ding'an Xiezhen met He Lingtu's force, broke it, pursued to Wutai, and took tens of thousands of heads.

sentences.zh: 明日，至蔚州，敵不敢出，斜軫書帛射城上，諭以招慰意。

translations.literal: The next day he reached Weizhou; the enemy dared not come out; Xiezhen shot a written cloth onto the wall to announce his intent to win them over.
translations.idiomatic: Next day he came to Weizhou; the foe would not sally; Xiezhen shot a message written on cloth onto the walls offering terms.

sentences.zh: 陰聞宋軍來救，令都監耶律題子夜伏兵險厄，俟敵至而發。

translations.literal: Secretly hearing that Song relief was coming, he ordered Commissioner Yelu Tizi to lie in ambush by night in a narrow pass to strike when the enemy arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Learning secretly that Song relief was on the way, he ordered Commissioner Yelu Tizi to hide troops by night in a defile and spring when the enemy came.

sentences.zh: 城守者見救至，突出。

translations.literal: The garrison, seeing rescue had come, burst out.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders, seeing help arrive, rushed out.

sentences.zh: 斜軫擊其背，二軍俱潰，追至飛狐，斬首二萬餘級，遂取蔚州。

translations.literal: Xiezhen struck their rear; both armies were routed; the pursuit reached Feihu, beheaded more than twenty thousand, and Weizhou was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Xiezhen hit them from behind; both hosts broke; the chase reached Feihu with more than twenty thousand heads, and Weizhou fell.

sentences.zh: 賀令圖、潘美復以兵來，斜軫逆於飛狐，擊敗之。

translations.literal: He Lingtu and Pan Mei came again with troops; Xiezhen met them at Feihu and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He Lingtu and Pan Mei returned with an army; Xiezhen met them at Feihu and routed them.

sentences.zh: 宋軍在渾源、應州者，皆棄城走。

translations.literal: Song troops at Hunyuan and Yingzhou all abandoned their cities and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Song forces at Hunyuan and Yingzhou all deserted their posts and ran.

sentences.zh: 斜軫聞繼業出兵，令蕭撻凜伏兵於路。

translations.literal: Xiezhen heard Jiye was marching out and ordered Xiao Talin to lie in ambush along the road.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Jiye was moving out, Xiezhen ordered Xiao Talin to set an ambush on the road.

sentences.zh: 明旦，繼業兵至，斜軫擁眾為戰勢。

translations.literal: At dawn Jiye's troops arrived; Xiezhen massed his host in battle array.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak Jiye's men came up; Xiezhen drew up his forces for battle.

sentences.zh: 繼業麾幟而前，斜軫佯退。

translations.literal: Jiye advanced under his banners; Xiezhen feigned retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Jiye moved forward beneath his standards; Xiezhen pretended to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 伏兵發，斜軫進攻，繼業敗走，至狼牙村，眾軍皆潰。

translations.literal: The ambush rose; Xiezhen pressed the attack; Jiye was defeated and fled; at Langya Village the whole army collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The ambush burst forth; Xiezhen closed in; Jiye was beaten and fled; at Langya Village the entire army dissolved.

sentences.zh: 繼業為流矢所中，被擒。

translations.literal: Jiye was struck by a stray arrow and captured.
translations.idiomatic: Jiye was hit by a stray arrow and taken alive.

sentences.zh: 斜軫責曰：「汝與我國角勝三十餘年，今日何面目相見！

translations.literal: Xiezhen reproached him, saying, "You have contested our state for more than thirty years—what face have you to meet me today!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiezhen rebuked him: "You have matched our realm for more than thirty years—how dare you show your face today!"

sentences.zh: 」繼業但稱死罪而已。

translations.literal: Jiye could only plead guilty unto death.
translations.idiomatic: Jiye could only confess his capital crime.

sentences.zh: 初，繼業在宋以驍勇聞，人號楊無敵，首建梗邊之策。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Song, Jiye had been famed for valor; men called him Yang the Invincible, and he first urged a hard border policy.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly in Song, Jiye was renowned for fierceness; people nicknamed him Yang the Invincible, and he first pressed a policy of stiff resistance on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 至狼牙村，心惡之，欲避不可得。

translations.literal: At Langya Village his heart loathed the place; he wished to avoid it but could not.
translations.idiomatic: At Langya Village he felt an ill omen about the name; he wished to turn aside but could not.

sentences.zh: 既擒，三日死。

translations.literal: Once captured, he died within three days.
translations.idiomatic: After his capture he died within three days.

sentences.zh: 斜軫歸闕，以功加守太保。

translations.literal: Xiezhen returned to court and, for his merit, was promoted to acting Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Xiezhen came back to the capital and, for his service, was advanced to acting Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 從太后南伐，卒於軍。

translations.literal: Following the empress dowager on a southern campaign, he died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the empress dowager on a southern expedition and died in camp.

sentences.zh: 太后親為哀臨，仍給葬具。

translations.literal: The empress dowager personally mourned him and also provided funeral goods.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager mourned him in person and furnished his burial.

sentences.zh: 庶子狗兒，官至小將軍。

translations.literal: His son by a concubine, Gou'er, reached the rank of junior general.
translations.idiomatic: A son by a concubine, Gou'er, rose to junior general.

sentences.zh: 耶律奚低

translations.literal: Yelu Xidi
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Xidi

sentences.zh: 耶律奚低，孟父楚國王之後。

translations.literal: Yelu Xidi was a descendant of the Prince of Chu, his father's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Xidi was descended from the Prince of Chu on his father's elder-brother line.

sentences.zh: 便弓馬，勇於攻戰。

translations.literal: Skilled with bow and horse, bold in attack and battle.
translations.idiomatic: He was adept with bow and horse and fierce in assault.

sentences.zh: 景宗時，多任以軍事。

translations.literal: In Emperor Jingzong's time he was often entrusted with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Jingzong he was repeatedly charged with military duties.

sentences.zh: 統和四年，為右皮室詳穩。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tonghe he was made right Pishi commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tonghe he became right Pishi commander.

sentences.zh: 時宋將楊繼業陷山西郡縣，奚低從樞密使斜軫討之。

translations.literal: When the Song general Yang Jiye overran the prefectures of Shanxi, Xidi followed Privy Councilor Xiezhen to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When Song general Yang Jiye seized the Shanxi prefectures, Xidi campaigned under Privy Councilor Xiezhen against him.

sentences.zh: 凡戰必以身先，矢無虛發。

translations.literal: In every battle he took the lead in person; no arrow he loosed missed.
translations.idiomatic: In every fight he led from the front, and every shaft he let fly found its mark.

sentences.zh: 繼業敗於朔州之南，匿深林中。

translations.literal: Jiye was defeated south of Shuozhou and hid in deep forest.
translations.idiomatic: Jiye was beaten south of Shuozhou and concealed himself in thick woods.

sentences.zh: 奚低望袍影而射，繼業墮馬。

translations.literal: Xidi shot at the shadow of a robe and Jiye fell from his horse.
translations.idiomatic: Xidi aimed at a robe's shadow and brought Jiye down from his horse.

sentences.zh: 先是，軍令須生擒繼業，奚低以故不能為功。

translations.literal: Earlier the army order required Jiye to be taken alive; for this reason Xidi could not claim the merit.
translations.idiomatic: An earlier army order had required Jiye alive, so Xidi could not win credit for the kill.

sentences.zh: 後太后南伐，屢有戰績。

translations.literal: Later, on the empress dowager's southern campaigns, he won repeated victories.
translations.idiomatic: On later southern campaigns under the empress dowager he won battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 以病卒。

translations.literal: He died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness.

sentences.zh: 耶律學古

translations.literal: Yelu Xuegu
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Xuegu

sentences.zh: 耶律學古，字乙辛隱，於越窪之庶孫。

translations.literal: Yelu Xuegu, style name Yixin, was a grandson by a concubine of Yuyue Wa.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Xuegu, whose style name was Yixin, was a grandson on the concubine line of Yuyue Wa.

sentences.zh: 穎悟好學，工譯鞮及詩。

translations.literal: Quick-witted and fond of learning, skilled in translating Kitan and in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and studious, he was adept at Kitan translation and at verse.

sentences.zh: 保寧中，補禦盞郎君。

translations.literal: In the Baoning era he was appointed attendant cup-bearer.
translations.idiomatic: During Baoning he was made attendant cup-bearer.

sentences.zh: 乾亨元年，宋既下河東，乘勝侵燕，學古受詔往援。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianheng, after Song had taken Hedong and pressed the advantage to invade Yan, Xuegu received orders to go to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianheng, once Song had conquered Hedong and, riding the momentum, invaded Yan, Xuegu was ordered to march to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 始至京，宋敗耶律奚底、蕭討古等，勢益張，圍城三周，穴地而進，城中民懷二心。

translations.literal: When he first reached the capital, Song had already defeated Yelu Xidi, Xiao Taogu, and others; their momentum grew; they besieged the city for three circuits, advanced by tunneling underground, and the people within wavered in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely reached Nanjing when Song had already routed Yelu Xidi and Xiao Taogu; their strength swelled; they invested the city for three full rounds, dug under the walls, and the townsfolk's hearts were divided.

sentences.zh: 學古以計安反側，隨宜備禦，晝夜不少懈。

translations.literal: Xuegu by stratagem settled those who wavered, made ready defenses as circumstances required, and never slackened day or night.
translations.idiomatic: Xuegu won over the wavering by policy, improvised defenses as needed, and never rested day or night.

sentences.zh: 適有敵三百餘人夜登城，學古戰卻之。

translations.literal: By chance more than three hundred of the enemy climbed the wall by night; Xuegu fought them off.
translations.idiomatic: Some three hundred of the enemy happened to scale the wall at night; Xuegu beat them back.

sentences.zh: 會援軍至，圍遂解。

translations.literal: When relief troops arrived the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Relief forces came up and the siege was broken.

sentences.zh: 學古開門列陣，四面鳴鼓，居民大呼，聲震天地。

translations.literal: Xuegu opened the gates and drew up battle lines; drums sounded on four sides; the populace shouted; the sound shook heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Xuegu threw open the gates and formed ranks; drums rolled on every side; the people roared until heaven and earth trembled.

sentences.zh: 旋有高梁之捷。

translations.literal: Soon came the victory at Gaoliang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long came triumph at Gaoliang River.

sentences.zh: 以功遙授保靜軍節度使，為南京馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed in absentia military commissioner of the Baojing Army and commander of Nanjing horse and foot forces.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was named in absentia military commissioner of the Baojing Army and made commander of Nanjing's horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 二年，伐宋，乞將漢軍，從之，改彰國軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year they attacked Song; he begged to lead Han troops and was granted it; he was made military commissioner of the Zhangguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, campaigning against Song, he asked to lead Han troops and was allowed; he was transferred to military commissioner of the Zhangguo Army.

sentences.zh: 時南境未靜，民思休息，學古禁寇掠以安之。

translations.literal: The southern border was not yet calm and the people longed for rest; Xuegu forbade raiding and plunder to reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: The south was still unsettled and the people craved peace; Xuegu banned looting to calm them.

sentences.zh: 會宋將潘美率兵分道來侵，學古以軍少，虛張旗幟，雜丁黃為疑兵。

translations.literal: When the Song general Pan Mei led troops by separate routes to invade, Xuegu's force was few; he displayed banners in false abundance and mixed laborers and the aged as decoy troops.
translations.idiomatic: Song general Pan Mei advanced along several routes; Xuegu had too few men, so he raised extra banners and mingled laborers and elders as dummy forces.

sentences.zh: 是夜，適獨虎峪舉烽火，遣人偵視，見敵俘掠村野，擊之，悉獲所掠物，擒其將領。

translations.literal: That night, as beacon fires were raised at Duhuyu alone, he sent men to reconnoiter, saw the enemy seizing and plundering villages, struck them, and recovered all that had been taken, capturing their officers.
translations.idiomatic: That night beacons flared at Duhuyu; he sent scouts, found the enemy plundering the countryside, attacked, recovered everything they had taken, and seized their commanders.

sentences.zh: 自是學古與潘美各守邊約，無相侵軼，民獲安業。

translations.literal: From then on Xuegu and Pan Mei each kept to the border pact without mutual raids, and the people could pursue their livelihoods in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Xuegu and Pan Mei each held to a border truce without incursions, and the people lived securely.

sentences.zh: 以功為惕隱，卒。

translations.literal: For his merit he was made tiyi and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was appointed tiyi and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 弟烏不呂。

translations.literal: His younger brother was Wubulü.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Wubulü.

translations.literal: 〈Supplement〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Appendix〉

sentences.zh: 烏不呂

translations.literal: Wubulü
translations.idiomatic: Wubulü

sentences.zh: 烏不呂，字留隱。

translations.literal: Wubulü, style name Liuyin.
translations.idiomatic: Wubulü, whose style name was Liuyin.

sentences.zh: 嚴重，有膂力，善屬文。

translations.literal: Stern and grave, with great physical strength, skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Grave in bearing, powerfully built, and skilled at writing.

sentences.zh: 統和中伐宋，屢任以軍事。

translations.literal: In the Tonghe campaigns against Song he was repeatedly entrusted with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tonghe wars against Song he was repeatedly given military command.

sentences.zh: 嘗與爻直不相能，因曰：「爾奴才，何所知？

translations.literal: Once he and Yaozhi did not get along, and he said, "You slave—what do you know?"
translations.idiomatic: He once clashed with Yaozhi and snapped, "You menial—what do you understand?"

sentences.zh: 」爻直訟於北院樞密使韓德讓。

translations.literal: Yaozhi sued him before Northern Court Privy Councilor Han Derang.
translations.idiomatic: Yaozhi brought suit before Northern Court Privy Councilor Han Derang.

sentences.zh: 德讓怒，問曰：「爾安得此奴耶？

translations.literal: Derang was angry and asked, "How dare you call a man such a slave?"
translations.idiomatic: Derang was furious and demanded, "How dare you call anyone a slave?"

sentences.zh: 」烏不呂對曰：「三父異籍時亦易得。

translations.literal: Wubulü answered, "In the time of the three fathers of different registers they were easy to come by too."
translations.idiomatic: Wubulü replied, "Even in the days of the three fathers with separate registers they were easy enough to obtain."

sentences.zh: 」德讓笑而釋之。

translations.literal: Derang laughed and released him.
translations.idiomatic: Derang laughed and let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 後從蕭恒德伐蒲盧毛朵部，以功為東路統軍都監。

translations.literal: Later he followed Xiao Hengde in campaigning against the Puloumaoduo tribe and, for his merit, was made eastern route army commander.
translations.idiomatic: Later, campaigning with Xiao Hengde against the Puloumaoduo tribe, he was made eastern route army commander for his service.

sentences.zh: 及德讓為大丞相，薦其材可任統軍使，太后曰：「烏不呂嘗不遜於卿，何善而薦？

translations.literal: When Derang became grand chancellor he recommended that Wubulü's talent suited the post of army commander; the empress dowager said, "Wubulü was once disrespectful to you—why do you recommend him so warmly?"
translations.idiomatic: When Derang rose to grand chancellor he urged that Wubulü was fit to be army commander; the empress dowager said, "Wubulü once showed you no deference—why praise him?"

sentences.zh: 」德讓奏曰：「臣忝相位，於臣猶不屈，況於其餘。

translations.literal: Derang memorialized, "Your servant is unworthy of the highest office; toward your servant he would not yield—how much less toward others."
translations.idiomatic: Derang answered, "I hold the highest office, yet he would not bend even to me—still less to anyone else."

sentences.zh: 以此知可用。

translations.literal: From this one knows he can be employed.
translations.idiomatic: By that token he is fit for use.

sentences.zh: 若任使之，必能鎮撫諸蕃。

translations.literal: If you appoint him, he will surely be able to pacify the various tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Put him in command and he will surely keep the frontier tribes in order.

sentences.zh: 」太后從之，加金紫崇祿大夫、檢校太尉。

translations.literal: The empress dowager followed this and added the titles Golden Purple Glory Grandee and acting Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager agreed and added Golden Purple Glory Grandee and acting Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 而弟國留以罪亡，烏不呂及其母俱下吏。

translations.literal: But his younger brother Guoliu fled after a crime, and Wubulü and his mother were both handed to the officials.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Guoliu, however, fled after a crime, and Wubulü and his mother were both arrested.

sentences.zh: 恐禍及母，陰使人召國留，紿曰：「太后知事之誣，汝第來勿畏。

translations.literal: Fearing disaster would reach his mother, he secretly sent for Guoliu, deceiving him, "The empress dowager knows the affair was false; come, brother, and do not fear."
translations.idiomatic: Afraid harm would fall on his mother, he secretly summoned Guoliu with a lie: "The empress dowager knows the charge is false—come, brother, and have no fear."

sentences.zh: 」國留至，送有司，坐誅。

translations.literal: When Guoliu arrived he was delivered to the authorities and executed for the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Guoliu came, was handed to the magistrates, and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 其後，退歸田里，以疾卒。

translations.literal: Afterward he retired to his village estate and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He later withdrew to his home district and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 論曰：宋乘下太原之銳，以師圍燕，繼遣曹彬、楊繼業等分道來伐。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Song, riding the sharp edge of its conquest of Taiyuan, sent armies to besiege Yan and then dispatched Cao Bin, Yang Jiye, and others by separate routes to attack.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal runs: Song, flush from taking Taiyuan, besieged Yan and then sent Cao Bin, Yang Jiye, and others along several routes.

sentences.zh: 是兩役也，遼亦岌岌乎殆哉！

translations.literal: In these two campaigns Liao too was in peril, nearly lost!
translations.idiomatic: In both campaigns Liao itself stood on the brink of ruin!

sentences.zh: 休哥奮擊於高梁，敵兵奔潰；

translations.literal: Xiuge struck fiercely at Gaoliang and the enemy army broke and fled;
translations.idiomatic: Xiuge smote them at Gaoliang until the foe broke and ran;

sentences.zh: 斜軫擒繼業於朔州，旋復故地。

translations.literal: Xiezhen captured Jiye at Shuozhou and soon recovered the old territory.
translations.idiomatic: Xiezhen took Jiye at Shuozhou and quickly restored the former lands.

sentences.zh: 宋自是不復深入，社稷固而邊境寧，雖配古名將，無愧矣。

translations.literal: Song from then on no longer penetrated deeply; the altars were secure and the border tranquil—matched against famed generals of antiquity, they need not blush.
translations.idiomatic: Song never again pushed deep inland; the state was firm and the frontier calm—set beside the great captains of old, they need not blush.

sentences.zh: 然非學古之在南京安其反側，則二將之功，蓋亦難致。

translations.literal: Yet had it not been for Xuegu settling those who wavered at Nanjing, the merit of the two generals would have been hard to achieve.
translations.idiomatic: Yet without Xuegu steadying Nanjing's divided hearts, the two generals' victories might never have come.

sentences.zh: 故曰國以人重，信哉！

translations.literal: Therefore it is said a state is heavy because of its men—how true!
translations.idiomatic: So it is said: a realm weighs on the men who serve it—indeed!
